operators.name: batchnorm2d_forward
semantics: Computes batch normalization in evaluation mode: y = (x - running_mean) / sqrt(running_var + eps) * weight + bias
Normalization is per channel C; x shape [N, C, H, W]
running_mean and running_var are per-channel constants
Supports arbitrary strides on x; output tensor has same strides as x
All inputs and outputs on CUDA device

operators.name: square_forward
semantics: Computes element-wise square: y = x * x
Preserves shape, dtype, device, and strides
Supports arbitrary strides

operators.name: avgpool2d_forward

returns.shape: [N, C, floor((H + 2*padding - kernel_size) / stride) + 1, floor((W + 2*padding - kernel_size) / stride) + 1]

semantics: Applies 2D average pooling over input [N, C, H, W]
Output spatial dimensions: floor((H + 2*padding - kernel_size) / stride) + 1
If count_include_pad is False, padding values are excluded from average denominator

Here count_include_pad is always False, matching PyTorch AvgPool2d default for non-zero padding? Actually PyTorch AvgPool2d default count_include_pad=True, but in reference model AvgPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0) has no padding, so count_include_pad has no effect. Therefore this parameter can be fixed to False in the binding but should be passed as False from model_new.py to match the contract.
Supports arbitrary strides on input; output is contiguous with standard strides [C*outH*outW, outH*outW, outW, 1]
BatchNorm2d in eval mode: y = (x - running_mean) / sqrt(running_var + eps) * weight + bias
Normalization per channel over spatial dimensions N*H*W
Output shape [512, 32, 64, 64], float32 CUDA
Element-wise square of each element
Output shape [512, 32, 64, 64], float32 CUDA
2D average pooling with kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0
Output shape [512, 32, 32, 32], float32 CUDA
Each output element is average of a 2x2 non-overlapping window (since stride=kernel_size)
Returns pooled tensor [512, 32, 32, 32], float32 CUDA
